$$

$$

f(x)=\frac{{6}^{x}{e}^{-6}}{x!}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =P(X\in \{0,1,2,3\}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2)+f(3) \\  & =\frac{{6}^{0}{e}^{-6}}{0!}+\frac{{6}^{1}{e}^{-6}}{1!}+\frac{{6}^{2}{e}^{-6}}{2!}+\frac{{6}^{3}{e}^{-6}}{3!} \\  & ≈0.151\end{aligned}
$$

probability mass function:\n\n$$\nf(x) = \\dfrac{\\lambda^x e^{-\\lambda}}{x!}, \\qquad x=0,1,2,3, \\ldots\n$$\n\nIf a random variable $X$ follows a Poisson distribution with rate $\\lambda,$ then we machine learning.\nThis course is divided into three main categories: linear algebra, multivariable calculus, and probability & statistics. Logical reasoning and Boolean functions are also studied, providing important conceptual motivation for understanding the expressive limitations of some simple machine learning models, such as why certain functions (e.g. XOR) cannot be represented by a single-layer neural network.\nStudents then explore matrices in-depth. They study Gaussian elimination, solve systems of equations, learn about determinants and their properties, and compute inverse matrices. These tools form the computational backbone of many machine learning algorithms.\nAs part of this course, students perform a deep dive into vector spaces, exploring linear independence, subspaces, bases, dimension, rank, and nullity.
